sara: Quick heads-up — after landing the fp8/int8 split fallback yesterday we're seeing ~12% p50 token latency bump on long-context prompts when KV cache hit rate < ~60%. Anyone seen this?

mike: Not on my radar. Do you have a profile or counters?

julia: Pushed a short flamegraph and kernel counters to the perf bucket: https://perf.internal/graphs/1782345 (private). Key snapshot below.

julia: ```
per_token_latency: {
  prefix_tokens: 40us,
  kv_lookup: 80us,
  kernel_exec: 220us,
  post_proc: 10us
}
kernel_counters: {
  fp8_kernels: 2345,
  int8_kernels: 112,
  int4_kernels: 18,
  kernel_switches: 78
}
kv_cache: hits=480 misses=320 hit_rate=60%
```

raj: That kernel_switches number stands out. Our batching heuristic flips to the fp8 path for batches > 8 or seq_len > 1024. If kv_hit_rate drops the effective end-to-end cost shifts and the scheduler might pick a different kernel mid-stream.

mike: Repro steps I used: `./bench_tool --model redwood/open-xxl --seq 2048 --batch 4 --seed 42 --warm 50 --iters 200 --kv-hit-rate 0.55`. See perf log:

mike: ```
[INFO] selected_kernel=fp8_avx2
[DEBUG] kv_cache_hit=false seq_idx=512
[WARN] kernel_switch (fp8->int8) at token=523 latency_delta=+28us
```

sara: Repro'd locally with that bench and got same kernel_switch pattern. Looks like calibration decision at runtime is being influenced by per-batch quantization stats that are noisy when cache_hit < threshold.

perf-bot: Automated alert: p50_token_latency increased by 11.8% for /v1/generate on model redwood/open-xxl in us-west-2 between 2026-03-12T02:00 and 2026-03-12T04:00.

julia: Probable root cause: the calibration step that estimates dynamic range for fp8 uses a suffix sample of recent activations. When KV cache is low, activation distribution shifts and the estimator triggers fallback which forces a kernel switch mid-seq. Kernel switches are expensive (cache flushes + recompile-ish work) and amplify per-token latency.

raj: Short-term mitigation: add an override to prefer int8 when kv_hit_rate < 0.7 for long-context routes. Longer term we should add a hysteresis window in the kernel selector and emit a `kernel_choice_confidence` counter.

mike: Also adding per-token kernel_id counter would help pinpoint exact token indices where switches happen. We currently only have per-request aggregated counters.

julia: Agreed. Proposed observability additions:
- per-token latency breakdown in console for sampled traces
- kernel_id histogram (per-token) exported to metrics backend
- kv_hit_ratio per-batch gauge (already exist, surface at route level)
- kernel_switch_count with labels {route, model, batch_size, kv_hit_bucket}

sara: For immediate testing I pushed a canary that forces `quant_fallback_threshold=0.75` for canary pool. Deploy-bot: can you confirm rollout status?

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: canary-pool-3 (10% traffic). Health checks OK. Rolling window 30m.

mike: After canary started I'm seeing kernel_switch_count down from 78->6 in the sampled traces and p50 token latency back to baseline. Initial numbers look promising.

julia: I'll open a small RFC for the selector hysteresis + counters. Also adding a small synthetic calibration test to the CI to avoid regressions.

sara: Thanks — next steps: (1) add per-token kernel_id counter + export, (2) selector hysteresis change + RFC, (3) CI synthetic calibration test. Assigning owners in the RFC.

raj: Will take (2). mike, can you own the metrics + dashboard?

mike: Yep. I’ll wire up the kernel_id histogram and a kv_hit_ratio panel in the route dashboard.

sara: Great. If anyone finds more repros please paste bench cmd+output here. :pray:
